Investors interested in stocks from the Internet - Software sector have probably already heard of Paycom Software (PAYC) and Cloudflare (NET). But which of these two companies is the best option for those looking for undervalued stocks? Let's take a closer look.

There are plenty of strategies for discovering value stocks, but we have found that pairing a strong Zacks Rank with an impressive grade in the Value category of our Style Scores system produces the best returns. The Zacks Rank is a proven strategy that targets companies with positive earnings estimate revision trends, while our Style Scores work to grade companies based on specific traits.

Both Paycom Software and Cloudflare have a Zacks Rank of #2 (Buy) right now. This system places an emphasis on companies that have seen positive earnings estimate revisions, so investors should feel comfortable knowing that these stocks have improving earnings outlooks. But this is just one piece of the puzzle for value investors.

Value investors also try to analyze a wide range of traditional figures and metrics to help determine whether a company is undervalued at its current share price levels.

Our Value category highlights undervalued companies by looking at a variety of key metrics, including the popular P/E ratio, as well as the P/S ratio, earnings yield, cash flow per share, and a variety of other fundamentals that have been used by value investors for years.

PAYC currently has a forward P/E ratio of 19.33, while NET has a forward P/E of 248.83. We also note that PAYC has a PEG ratio of 1.01. This metric is used similarly to the famous P/E ratio, but the PEG ratio also takes into account the stock's expected earnings growth rate. NET currently has a PEG ratio of 6.12.

Another notable valuation metric for PAYC is its P/B ratio of 15.84. The P/B ratio pits a stock's market value against its book value, which is defined as total assets minus total liabilities. For comparison, NET has a P/B of 77.93.

Based on these metrics and many more, PAYC holds a Value grade of B, while NET has a Value grade of F.

Both PAYC and NET are impressive stocks with solid earnings outlooks, but based on these valuation figures, we feel that PAYC is the superior value option right now.

title: What Did Cloudflare Stock Investors Miss Before The Run?
detail:
What Did Cloudflare Stock Investors Miss Before The Run?
Trefis Team

NET
^GSPC

ZS
PANW
Explore stocks on Coinbase

For questions about this article or underlying research, email help@trefis.com.

Cloudflare (NET) stock rose 63.5% between May 13 and November 11, 2026, outpacing the 2.9% gain for the S&P 500. Sales growth accelerated during those months, and management credited its Workers Developer Platform and AI agent workloads across its network. The run appears surprising only if the AI demand behind Workers remained hidden until May. So when did AI demand for Workers first show up?

Cloudflare Tied Workers To AI In Early 2025

Management made this connection out loud on the call for the fourth quarter of 2024, held on February 6, 2025: "The killer application for Cloudflare Workers is turning out to be AI." On the same call, management said Workers could become the first choice for developers seeking the best price for performance. That statement arrived more than a year before the six months measured here.

On November 17, 2025, Cloudflare agreed to acquire Replicate, an AI platform that helps developers deploy and run AI models. So by late 2025, the company was putting money, not just words, behind AI for developers.

Did Cloudflare's Filed Quarters Show Faster Growth?

Yes, for three quarters in a row. Revenue growth against a year earlier rose from 26.5% in the quarter ended March 2025 to 33.6% in the quarter ended December 2025, and each quarter in between was faster than the one before. All of those quarters were filed before May 13, 2026.

The release for the December quarter, published on February 10, 2026, added a sign about new business. Cloudflare said it had closed its biggest contract ever by yearly value, averaging $42.5 million a year. The company also said new annual contract value grew nearly 50% from a year earlier. Then growth paused: revenue rose 33.5% in the quarter ended March 2026, roughly matching the pace of the quarter before.

What Had Changed At Cloudflare By November?

Growth had sped up again. Revenue rose 39.2% from a year earlier in the quarter ended September 2026. This pace came well above the March quarter's rate, and it represented growth across the entire company rather than a single product line. Peers did not move as one group during the same six months: Palo Alto Networks gained 46.8%, while Akamai Technologies fell 46.2%.

The 63.5% gain came after a fall. Every one of the signs from 2025 and early 2026 was public by May 13, and in the six months before that date Cloudflare stock fell 14.6%. So reading the signs early meant holding through that fall before the figures sped up again.

Shares of Penguin Solutions, Inc. PENG have surged 161.6% over the past year, vastly outperforming the Internet – Software industry's 0.7% decline and the broader Computer and Technology sector's 8.6% gain.

The stock has even outpaced major peers like Cloudflare NET, Snowflake SNOW and AudioEye AEYE. During this time frame, shares of Cloudflare, Snowflake and AudioEye have returned 47.6%, 17.3% and 16.7%, respectively.

PENG's Stock Performance
Zacks Investment Research

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Strong demand for AI infrastructure, accelerating memory sales and improving profitability have fueled PENG's rally. However, after such an exceptional run, the question is whether Penguin Solutions' customer pipeline, earnings revisions and valuation still offer meaningful upside or whether execution risks warrant caution. Let's dive deep.

AI Factory Platform Strengthens PENG's Growth Prospects

Penguin Solutions' Full-Stack AI Factory Platform positions it at the intersection of artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure and memory, two areas benefiting from increasingly demanding inference workloads. Rather than merely supplying servers, the company integrates ComputeAI systems, MemoryAI solutions, OriginAI reference architectures, ClusterWareAI software and services covering infrastructure design, deployment and ongoing management. This breadth allows Penguin Solutions to support enterprises and neocloud providers throughout the AI data center lifecycle.

ClusterWareAI provides monitoring, GPU health management and automated remediation, while newer agentic capabilities aim to simplify operations and improve utilization. The software-and-services component could deepen customer relationships and create longer-duration revenue opportunities alongside hardware deployments. PENG's designation as an NVIDIA AI Factory Specialized Partner also reinforces its credibility in delivering complex GPU infrastructure, although successful execution remains essential.

Customer momentum offers tangible evidence of traction. Penguin Solutions secured six new AI infrastructure customers in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, including four neocloud providers. Across fiscal 2026, it added 17 customers and expanded engagements with 12 others. Notably, one multiyear agreement involves deploying and operating a 36,000-GPU AI factory in Norway. These wins could generate follow-on opportunities as customers expand capacity and adopt managed services, although bookings will convert into revenues only as deployments progress.

$1,000 Split Across These 3 Cybersecurity Stocks Could Be Worth This Much in 5 Years
Micah Zimmerman, The Motley Fool
Thu, November 12, 2026 at 5:23 AM PST 5 min read
CRWD
FTNT
NET
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Here's a simple way to think about cybersecurity stocks right now: Companies are handing more of their work to artificial intelligence, and hackers are using AI more, too. That turns robust cybersecurity from a nice-to-have into the essential lock on the front door, and three companies in that industry just shared news that hints at where they'll be in five years.

Split an investment of $1,000 evenly across Fortinet (NASDAQ: FTNT), Cloudflare (NYSE: NET), and CrowdStrike (NASDAQ: CRWD), and you'd put about $333 into each. In my base cases for how those stocks will perform, that $1,000 would grow to roughly $1,500 by late 2031. These are my own scenarios, built on how fast I expect their sales to grow each year and what valuations investors will be willing to pay for them.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Image source: Getty Images.
The firewall sale is just the down payment

Fortinet sells firewalls -- the boxes that decide what gets into a company's network. On Oct. 28, it reported third-quarter revenue up 20% to $2.08 billion, with product sales, mostly hardware, up 37%. But it trimmed its forecast for service revenue -- the subscriptions that customers continue to pay after they buy the boxes -- to a range of $5.15 billion to $5.17 billion, down from $5.18 billion to $5.22 billion three months earlier. The stock sold off hard and now trades around $122, down from a 52-week high near $197.

I think the market is reading that backward. CFO Christiane Ohlgart said big new customers switch on their subscriptions in stages, and pointed out that service billings, which offer an early look at future subscription revenue, grew by 26%. Management also expects service revenue to grow faster in 2027 than in 2026.

My five-year scenario: Fortinet sales will grow at an annualized rate of 12% a year, well below this year's pace, and investors will pay 20% less per dollar of sales than today. That would turn a $333 stake into one worth roughly $470.

Free locks today, paying customers tomorrow

Cloudflare runs a giant network in front of millions of websites, blocking attacks and speeding up traffic. On Nov. 5, it reported third-quarter revenue up 39% to $782.5 million, its fastest growth rate in nearly four years. It added more than 158,000 paying customers in the quarter, and developers building on its platform jumped from 7 million to 10 million in three months.

PANW vs. NET: Which Cybersecurity Stock Should You Buy Right Now?

Palo Alto Networks, Inc. PANW and Cloudflare, Inc. NET are both at the forefront of the cybersecurity space, playing key roles in guarding organizations from extensive cyberattacks. PANW focuses broadly on next-generation firewalls, cloud security and AI-driven threat detection. Cloudflare provides a cloud-native platform spanning network security, application security and connectivity.

Both PANW and NET are riding key industry trends, driven by the mounting incidents of credential theft, remote desktop protocol breaches and social engineering-based strikes by malicious actors. However, from an investment point of view, one stock offers a more favorable outlook than the other right now. Let's break down their fundamentals, growth prospects, market challenges and valuation to determine which stock offers a more compelling investment case.

The Case for PANW Stock

Palo Alto Networks remains a cybersecurity leader, offering solutions for network security, cloud security and endpoint solutions for customers who need full enterprise security support. Its next-generation firewalls and advanced threat detection technologies are widely recognized and adopted globally.

Palo Alto Networks' wide range of innovative products, strong customer base and growing opportunities in areas like Zero Trust, Secure Access Service Edge (SASE) and private 5G security continue to support its long-term growth potential. For instance, the company's SASE bookings grew 40% in fiscal 2026, supported by growth across Access, SD-WAN and secure browser. PANW displaced legacy vendors in nearly 100 customer accounts, representing more than $400 million in total contract value. The displacement volume was nearly double that of the prior year.

PANW's SASE business is benefiting from strong customer demand for cloud-delivered networking and security solutions as enterprises continue to support hybrid work environments and secure access to cloud applications. The company integrates SASE with its firewall, SD-WAN and other security products, allowing existing customers to add SASE without bringing in another vendor. Management said this makes platform standardization a simpler choice for customers. In the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, a global telecom leader signed a $126 million agreement to expand its next-generation firewall footprint while replacing legacy proxy providers with Prisma Access for SASE.

However, PANW's non-GAAP gross margin fell 100 basis points year over year to 74.8% in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, while non-GAAP gross margin for fiscal 2026 declined 60 basis points to 75.8%. The decline was mainly due to the growing mix of SaaS offerings, which are still scaling toward mature margin levels. Management expects cloud hosting costs to grow faster than revenues in fiscal 2027, which could weigh on gross-margin expansion.

From Legacy Delivery Network to Enterprise Security Architecture

Akamai's revenue mix shows an operational shift that headline selling has overlooked. In the third quarter, revenue reached $1.12 billion with operating income rising to $111.4 million, lifting diluted earnings per share to $0.77. Security revenue rose 10% to $604 million in the second quarter, led by enterprise adoption of Guardicore microsegmentation and API protection, and is on track to top $2.4 billion for the full year.

Commercial validation backs that pivot. Operating cash flow reached $1.44 billion over the trailing twelve months with net income of $387.9 million. title: How Big Could Cloudflare Stock's Next Fall Be?
detail:
How Big Could Cloudflare Stock's Next Fall Be?
Trefis Team

Cloudflare (NET) stock lost 12.8% in the month to November 10, 2026, against 3.6% for the S&P 500, in a month when Akamai Technologies, Zscaler and Palo Alto Networks also fell. Buyers still pay 40 times the company's sales over the past year, betting that its growth keeps accelerating and its reported losses turn into profits. When markets sold off before, how much did Cloudflare stock give up, and for how long?

How Deep Did Cloudflare Stock Fall In Past Sell-Offs?

The 2022 inflation shock hit Cloudflare stock hardest: it fell 69%, while the S&P 500 fell 24%. Its largest fall at any time since its listing was deeper still: 82.6%, from its close on November 18, 2021, to its close on November 9, 2022. The market figures in this section are measured on the SPY fund, which tracks the index. Across the six market shocks the stock has traded through since its 2019 listing, it lost 30.7% on average, against 16.8% for the index. It fell further than the S&P 500 in all but one of them, the 2020 COVID-19 crash. The most recent, the 2025 tariff shock, took 40% off the stock against 19% off the index.

Cloudflare stock eventually returned to its pre-decline high every time. The median climb back from the low took 1.2 months, but recovering from the 2022 fall took 31.4 months, from its June 2022 low until January 2025. The stock closed lower still in November 2022 before that climb.

Cloudflare's Sales Are Growing Faster Than A Year Ago

Revenue rose 39.2% from a year earlier in fiscal Q3 2026, against 30.7% growth in the same quarter of 2025, so the faster growth buyers are counting on has held so far. Management said the quarter's growth came in particular from its Workers Developer Platform, from AI agent workloads across its network and from its largest customers. Customers that management counts as large brought in 75% of revenue, up from 73% a year earlier.

Cloudflare Still Reports Losses, And Gross Margin Is Slipping

Based on the figures in its filings, Cloudflare still lost money in fiscal Q3 2026. Its operating loss was 7.3% of revenue, slightly wider than the 6.7% of revenue reported a year earlier. On management's adjusted measure, the operating margin reached 17.5%, the highest in the company's history.

Management expects Cloudflare to turn a GAAP profit in fiscal Q4 2026, arriving earlier than the 2028 deadline it set at its 2026 Investor Day. That profit remains a forecast.

Gross margin is lower than a year ago. Management said the adjusted measure fell to 72.4% in fiscal Q3 2026, down 290 basis points from a year earlier. That level remains inside the company's long-term target range of 70% to 77%. Management also said its Workers product has slightly lower gross margins than products such as Zero Trust, though it costs much less to sell.
